title: Large-scale Neuron Community Discovery Reveals Neuron-Sparse Behaviors in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.23112v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: What reusable units of computation can we discover within a language model's neurons? Prior work has shown that individual forward passes can often be sparsified post-hoc to small groups of neurons, but it has been unclear whether these groups form coherent computational entities reused across inputs. We introduce neuron community discovery, an unsupervised method for finding neuron groups that recur across prompts and are causally necessary and sufficient, within the layers they span, for common computations. The method combines gradient-based attribution, a graph connecting neurons that are repeatedly attributed together, and community detection. Applied to Llama-3.1-8B using ten million prompts, it discovers thousands of candidate communities. translated_title: 大规模神经元社区发现揭示语言模型中的神经元稀疏行为
translated_abstract: 在语言模型的神经元中，我们能发现哪些可复用的计算单元？先前的研究表明，单次前向传播通常可以在事后被稀疏化为小型神经元群组，但这些群组是否构成跨输入复用的连贯计算实体仍不清楚。我们提出了神经元社区发现，这是一种无监督方法，用于寻找跨提示反复出现、且在其所跨越的层范围内对常见计算既因果必要又因果充分的神经元群组。该方法结合了基于梯度的归因分析、连接反复被共同归因的神经元的图结构，以及社区检测。将该方法应用于 Llama-3.1-8B 并使用一千万条提示，它发现了数千个候选社区。我们通过三项因果测试在保留提示上评估它们：社区必要性、层子集内的充分性以及层必要性。这些测试识别出了那些移除后会破坏计算功能的神经元群组。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种无监督的“神经元社区发现”方法，通过梯度归因、图构建和社区检测，在大语言模型中找出跨输入复用且因果必要充分的神经元群组，从而证明语言模型中存在可复用的稀疏神经元计算单元。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces "neuron community discovery," an unsupervised method combining gradient-based attribution, graph construction, and community detection to identify causally necessary and sufficient neuron groups reused across prompts, revealing reusable neuron-sparse computational units in large language models.
